features.title: Tripled c-pawns meet the doubled-pawn rule
features.reason: Three Black pawns occupy c, so that file meets the rule's at-least-two threshold.

features.title: Doubled c-pawns after the recapture
features.reason: White's c2 and c4 pawns are doubled; White has three pawn-file runs and Black has two.

features.title: The bishop occupies the supported d5 outpost
features.source: Gligoric - Gheorghiu, Tel Aviv 1966, after 19.Bxd5 in the 17...cxd5 line
features.reason: The bishop is on White's fifth rank, the e4 pawn defends d5, and no Black pawn is adjacent-file and in front.

features.title: The adjacent f-pawn excludes a backward e-pawn
features.reason: Black's e7 stop square e6 is attacked, but its f7 neighbour is on the same relative rank and fails the backward-pawn condition.

features.title: Pawn islands in the closed-center structure
features.reason: White's pawns span files a–d and f–h, two maximal runs; Black's occupy two runs.

features.title: The c3/c4 pawn pair is doubled
features.reason: White has pawns on c3 and c4, while Black has only one pawn on c.

features.title: The isolated d-pawn in the isolani position
features.reason: White's d4 pawn has no friendly pawn on c or e; Black's e6 pawn is not isolated because f7 is occupied.

features.title: File runs in the minority-attack position
features.reason: White's pawns span files a–b and d–h, two maximal runs; Black's span a–d and f–h.

features.title: The d6 pawn has a clear path
features.reason: White's d6 pawn has no Black pawn ahead on d or either adjacent file.

features.title: Two pawns do not form the defined chain
features.reason: The d4 and e5 pawns defend diagonally, but the maximal run has only two pawns, below the three-pawn definition.

features.title: Isolated edge pawns and a connected-file near miss
features.reason: White's a4 and Black's h5 have no friendly pawn on adjacent files; d4 is adjacent to White's e3 pawn.

features.title: Doubled pawns for both colours
features.reason: White has two c-pawns and Black has two f-pawns; White has only one pawn on e.

features.title: A backward pawn for each colour
features.reason: White d4 and Black g5 each have an adjacent-file pawn ahead and an empty stop square attacked by an enemy pawn; White e5 lacks the rank condition.

features.title: Only the front doubled pawn is passed
features.reason: The front d6 pawn is selected while d5 is not passed because d6 is in front on its file; b5 also blocks a4.

features.title: Two white runs of connected passers; Black has a one-file gap
features.reason: White has two maximal runs of adjacent-file passers; Black's b3 and d3 passers are separated by c.

features.title: Pawn-island counts for both colours
features.reason: White has the a-file and c-d runs; Black has the c- and f-file runs.

features.title: No pawn means no pawn islands
features.reason: Neither side has a pawn, so the required at-least-one-pawn condition fails.

features.title: Three-pawn chain versus a two-pawn run
features.reason: White's e4-d5-c6 chain has three defending pawns; Black's e5-d4 run stops at two.

features.title: Three-pawn chain for Black
features.reason: Black's e5-d4-c3 pawns defend each next pawn forward; White's two-pawn run is too short.

features.title: Kingside rights for both sides
features.reason: The FEN retains each king's kingside right but neither queenside right.

features.title: Queenside rights for both sides
features.reason: The FEN retains each king's queenside right but neither kingside right.

features.title: Castling rights absent without castling flags
features.reason: No castling flag is present, so neither side retains either right.

features.title: King-shield gaps for both colours
features.reason: Both kings are on relative rank one and their own e-file has no pawn on either of the next two ranks.

features.title: A pawn in front closes each shield gap
features.reason: Each king has its own pawn on the first square in front, so the two-square gap condition fails.

features.title: Open king files for both colours
features.reason: Neither colour has a pawn on either king's e-file.

features.title: A king file with a pawn is not open
features.reason: Both e-files contain pawns, so neither king's file is open.

features.title: Half-open king files for both colours
features.reason: Each king's file lacks its owner's pawn and contains at least one opposing pawn.

features.title: An own pawn defeats the half-open condition
features.reason: White's e2 pawn means its king file does not lack a White pawn.

features.title: Two attackers reach White's king zone
features.reason: Black's rook and knight attack e2 next to White's king; White's rook attacks Black's king on h8.

features.title: A distant slider is outside the king zone
features.reason: The bishop on a8 attacks no square occupied by or adjacent to White's king on e1.

features.title: Opposite-coloured bishop pairs
features.reason: Each side has one bishop on a light square and one on a dark square.

features.title: Same-coloured bishops are not a pair
features.reason: White's bishops on c1 and e3 occupy squares of the same colour.

features.title: Rooks on open files for both sides
features.reason: The a- and h-files have no pawns; White's d2 pawn keeps the d-file closed.

features.title: No pawns on a rook's file is open, not half-open
features.reason: File f has neither a White nor a Black pawn, so it is not half-open.

features.title: Half-open rook files for both sides
features.reason: White's d-file lacks a White pawn but has Black's d6 pawn; the e-file is the reverse.

features.title: A rook file without an opposing pawn is not half-open
features.reason: File f contains no Black pawn, failing the half-open-file condition.

features.title: Seventh-rank rooks for both colours
features.reason: Each rook is on its owner's relative seventh rank while the opposing king is on relative rank eight.

features.title: A sixth-rank rook misses the seventh-rank rule
features.reason: White's rook is on relative rank six, not rank seven.

features.title: Pawn-defended outposts for both colours
features.reason: The pieces are on relative ranks five, defended by friendly pawns, with no adjacent-file enemy pawn in front.

features.title: A rank-three piece is not an outpost
features.reason: The defended knight is on White's relative third rank, below the required fourth-to-sixth range.

features.title: A bad bishop with blocked same-colour pawns
features.reason: Black's c8 bishop colour has four Black pawns, all blocked by White pawns; White's b1 bishop colour has no White pawns.

features.title: One blocked pawn is below the bad-bishop threshold
features.reason: Black has a light-square pawn majority but only c6 is blocked by an opposing pawn.

features.title: Mobility lead for White
features.reason: White's bishop and knight attack 7 and 2 squares; the rook attacks h2–h8 and the enemy king on g1, totaling 17.

features.title: Mobility lead for Black
features.reason: Black's bishop and knight attack 7 and 2 squares; the rook attacks h7–h1 and the enemy king on g8, totaling 17.

features.title: Mobility lead at threshold minus one
features.reason: The bishop and knight contribute seven and two eligible squares, totaling nine rather than ten.

features.title: Space lead at three
features.reason: White's c3, d3 and e3 pawns each stand in front of one eligible rank-two square; Black has none.

features.title: Space lead for Black at three
features.reason: Black's c6, d6 and e6 pawns each stand in front of one eligible rank-four square; White has none.

features.title: Space lead at threshold minus one
features.reason: White has only two eligible squares in front of pawns, below the required difference of three.

features.title: Development lead at two
features.reason: Black has two undeveloped minor pieces and White has none, meeting the two-piece threshold.

features.title: Development lead for Black at two
features.reason: White has two undeveloped minor pieces and Black has none, meeting the two-piece threshold for Black.

features.title: Development lead at threshold minus one
features.reason: Black has one more undeveloped minor piece, below the required difference of two.

features.title: Material lead for White
features.reason: White's rook is worth five and Black's knight three, a material difference of two.

features.title: Material lead for Black
features.reason: Black's queen is worth nine and White's rook five, a material difference of four.

features.title: Equal rook material is not a lead
features.reason: Each side has one rook and no other material, so neither side is ahead.

features.title: White is up the exchange
features.reason: White has more rooks and Black has more knights plus bishops.

features.title: Black is up the exchange
features.reason: Black has more rooks and White has more knights plus bishops.

features.title: A rook advantage without a minor-piece advantage
features.reason: White has more rooks, but Black does not have more knights and bishops because neither side has a minor piece.

features.title: Pawn-file runs after the central exchange
features.reason: White's a-b and e-h pawn files and Black's a-d and f-h files each make two maximal runs.

features.title: Pawn islands in the Sicilian structure
features.reason: White's a-c and e-h files and Black's a-b and d-h files each form two maximal pawn runs.

features.title: A white bad bishop with two blocked same-colour pawns
features.reason: White's dark-square bishop has two dark-square pawns blocked by Black pawns, and no White pawn on the other colour.

features.title: Black connected passed pawns on adjacent files
features.reason: Black's b3 and c3 pawns are passed and form one maximal consecutive-file run.

features.title: White king shield gap on relative rank two
features.reason: White's king is on relative rank two and has no White pawn on e3 or e4.

features.title: Black king shield gap on relative rank two
features.reason: Black's king is on relative rank two and has no Black pawn on e6 or e5.

features.title: A king on relative rank three is outside the shield rule
features.reason: White's king on relative rank three exceeds the rule's k ≤ 2 limit.

features.title: A rank-four white outpost
features.reason: White's knight on relative rank four is defended by d3, with no enemy pawn on an adjacent file ahead.

features.title: A rank-four black outpost
features.reason: Black's knight on relative rank four is defended by d6, with no enemy pawn on an adjacent file ahead.

features.title: A rank-six white outpost
features.reason: White's knight on relative rank six is defended by d5, with no enemy pawn on an adjacent file ahead.

features.title: A rank-six black outpost
features.reason: Black's knight on relative rank six is defended by d4, with no enemy pawn on an adjacent file ahead.

features.title: A backward-pawn near miss without an attacked stop square
features.reason: White e4 has White d5 ahead on an adjacent file, but the e5 stop square is not attacked by a Black pawn.

lines.title: A rook arrives on an open file
lines.reason: The rook leaves the pawn-blocked b-file for the pawnless a-file and remains there.

lines.title: A rook leaves one open file and enters another
lines.reason: The a-file identity disappears and is absent at line end; the b-file identity appears and remains.

lines.title: Kingside castling removes the right
lines.reason: White's castling identity disappears and is absent at line end.

lines.title: Advancing a passer preserves its file identity
lines.reason: The pawn remains passed on file e after advancing, and §5 reports no change when its identity persists.

lines.title: A rook move on one open file is persistent
lines.reason: The rook remains on the same pawnless file, so its file-based identity persists without a change.

lines.title: A changing mobility value keeps its identity
lines.reason: White's mobility lead remains above ten as its value changes, and identity is tag plus side rather than value.

lines.title: A rook returns to an open file by line end
lines.reason: The a-file identity returns by line end, so its earlier disappearance does not hold at end; b-file appears only temporarily.
